To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Dakota Formation records a long-term, overall relative sea-level rise that was punctuated by brief relative sea-level falls and that high-frequency relative sea level changes were controlled by eustasy.

(1) the Dakota units represent high-frequency sequences, (2) the high-frequency sequences were probably eustatically controlled, (3) the high-frequency relative eustatic sea level fluctuations were probably related to the Milankovitch band and (4) the low-frequency sequences are probably related to the flexural response of the basin to tectonic subsidence and/or eustatic sea levels.

the Dakota units, which are interpreted as high-frequency sequences, were controlled by eustasy, whereas the overall retrogradational stacking pattern of the Dakota units reflects a long-term, eustatic sea level rise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay of tectonics and eustasy during the Early Cenomanian in the Sevier foreland basin.
the recognition of sequence stratigraphic patterns in the Cretaceous Dakota Formation of southern Utah and their correlation with global eustasy.
the interplay of eutasy and tectonic processes during the early stage of foreland basin evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Cretaceous Sevier orogenic foredeep was filled during the Early Cenomanian by the deposition of fluvial and shallow-marine sediments in response to the interaction of long- and short-term eustatic fluctuations, controlled by the Milankovitch band, and tectonism.
the Cenomanian sea-level fluctuations in the Kaiparowits Plateaus were controlled mainly by eustasy, with a significant contribution by tectonics.
the Dakota Formation is an excellent example of the interaction of tectonics and eustasy in a foreland setting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
eustasy, rather than tectonics, was the dominant control on relative sea-level changes in the Dakota Formation.

the Dakota Formation records the initial stage of the Cretacous Sevier foreland basin development in Utah and that it documents the interplay of tectonic and climatic processes during the initial phase.
the Cenomanian foredeep was filled by the Dakota Formation during the first phase of the Cretaceoous Sevier orogeny in response to flexural subsidence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the high-frequency sea-level cycles of the Cretaceus, as recorded in the Dakota, are not a product of the flexural response of the foreland basin to the tectonic activity of the Sevier thrust belt, but were controlled by eustatic sea level changes.
, even in the absence of a complete stratigraphic record, the interplay of epeirogenic and glacioeustasy is recorded in the stratigraphy of foreland basins.

the Cenomanian sea-level record in the Dakota Formation of southern Utah shows that high-frequency relative sea level changes were controlled by eustasy, and that the high-frequency sea level fluctuations were probably related to climate-driven eustatic changes.
